name: Classifying Behavior & Understanding the Product
description: The analytical groundwork before any design intervention begins. Covers product clarification (defining the product's purpose, target outcome, target actor, and target action) and target user definition via personas. Without accurately classifying the target behavior and understanding who performs it, behavioral interventions are misdirected.

subskills.name: Clarify the Product
subskills.description: Articulating what the product does at a fundamental level — its core value proposition, problem domain, and category. Ensures alignment across stakeholders before behavior classification begins. Often involves a product brief, one-sentence elevator pitch, or problem statement workshop.

subskills.name: Define Target Outcome
subskills.description: Identifying the specific, measurable state the product aims to bring the user to. The target outcome is distinct from the product's features — it describes the user's world after successful interaction. Requires distinguishing between business outcomes (revenue, retention) and user outcomes (skill gained, task completed).

subskills.name: Define Target Actor
subskills.description: Identifying who performs the target behavior — their role, context, motivation level, existing habits, and relationship with the product. Involves segmentation by behavioral profile rather than just demographic data. Distinct from personas in that it focuses on behavioral capacity and motivation.

subskills.name: Define Target Action
subskills.description: Specifying the exact behavior the design intervention aims to produce — as a concrete, observable, single action rather than a vague intention. Applies Fogg's behavior classification to determine if the action is a one-time, recurring, or permanent behavior.

subskills.name: Define Target Users — Personas
subskills.description: Creating behavioral personas that capture user goals, motivations, pain points, mental models, and behavioral tendencies. Distinguishes between proto-personas (assumption-based) and research-backed personas. Covers Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD) as an alternative framing focused on functional and emotional jobs.

github.signal: Persona documents, JTBD artifacts, or behavioral segmentation frameworks in repository
Product brief, problem statement, or design scope documentation
github.pattern: target outcome|target actor|target action|product brief|value proposition|problem statement

cv.signal: Conducted user research, persona creation, or behavioral segmentation for product teams
Defined product scope, target behaviors, or behavioral goals for design projects

linkedin.signal: User research, persona design, or Jobs-to-be-Done endorsed
Product strategy, behavioral design, or outcome-based design mentioned

junior.description: Can articulate the product's purpose clearly and create research-backed or proto-personas capturing user goals and motivations.

mid.description: Precisely defines target outcomes (user vs business), specifies behavioral actors by motivation and capacity, and articulates single observable target actions.

senior.description: Facilitates cross-functional alignment workshops on product purpose and behavioral goals; champions outcome-over-output design culture; integrates JTBD as organizational standard.
